projects.title: Parametric Exoskeleton Building
projects.description: A twisting, tapering tower organized around a public passage, with an exterior exoskeleton and selected floors that bridge across the opening.

blocks.text: For ARCH655 Project 1, I developed a parametric tower study organized around a tall public passage. The design brings together a twisting, tapering building mass, a curved exterior exoskeleton, and floor plates that respond to a large cut through the form. The passage is treated as a spatial experience in its own right: it opens views through the tower and creates moments where circulation and shared terraces meet.

The main design question is how a strong vertical opening can remain legible while the tower still reads as one connected structure. The exoskeleton follows the changing profile and gives the building a continuous outer frame. At the passage, most floor slabs stop at the cut. Every third slab spans all the way across, forming a periodic bridge between the two sides while leaving the intervening levels open. This lets the opening read as a deliberate void rather than a continuous slot filled by floor plates.
Before and after: the curve that defines the cut

The highlighted guide curve is the design input for the passage. Its path through the tower sets where the vertical opening moves and changes direction. In the resulting model, the cut follows that route; most floor slabs stop at the opening, while every third slab spans across it as a bridge. The after view hides the guide curve so the resulting passage is easier to read.

blocks.text: Four precedents helped frame the study. [The Klein Bottle House](https://www.mcbridecharlesryan.com.au/project/klein-bottle-house/) uses a spiral that passes back through itself to shape a sequence of spaces. [Arnhem Central Transfer Terminal](https://www.archdaily.com/777495/arnhem-central-transfer-terminal-unstudio) connects movement and form through a twisting structure and a continuous transition between interior and exterior. [One Thousand Museum](https://www.odparchitects.com/project/one-thousand-museum/) makes its curving exoskeleton a defining part of the tower structure and identity. [Morpheus Hotel](https://www.archdaily.com/896433/morpheus-hotel-zaha-hadid-architects) uses carved vertical voids, an atrium, and bridges to connect public spaces through a high-rise. I used these projects as reference points for continuity, circulation, and structure, then combined those ideas in a new design rather than reproducing a single precedent.

The Rhino and Grasshopper definition turns the design into a set of adjustable relationships. Controls for the tower profile, twist, taper, passage dimensions, and floor rhythm let me compare options while keeping the main design logic intact. The definition is grouped by function, with labeled controls and notes that make it easier to trace how each input affects the geometry. Changing the passage or tower profile updates the surrounding structure, while the every-third-floor rule preserves the intended pattern of open levels and bridges.

blocks.content: The oblique view makes the passage depth and the relationship between the exterior frame and floor slabs easier to read.
blocks.caption: Elevated view of the parametric tower, exoskeleton, floor plates, and passage.

blocks.text: The analysis is built into a separate Grasshopper definition, project1_analyses.gh, using the tower loft surface as its input. An Area component reports the surface area and centroid. Divide Surface samples the loft at 11 by 11 UV locations (121 points); those locations feed Principal Curvature and Surface Curvature, which report maximum and minimum principal curvature, their direction vectors, and Gaussian and mean curvature. A Bounding Box, followed by domain decomposition and subtraction, measures the tower overall X, Y, and Z extents. These outputs document the surface geometry and curvature directly in Grasshopper. The companion Rhino file, project1_analyses.3dm, contains a separate analysis group with the curvature visualization, dimensions, and labels.

The AI images explore how the passage, terraces, and exterior frame might come together as an architectural whole. They helped establish a visual direction for the parametric model, especially the contrast between a glazed tower surface and an open, planted route through its center. These are AI-generated concept images; they communicate an imagined design and should be read separately from screenshots of the Rhino and Grasshopper model.
